items.name: System Time(HH:MM:SS)
items.tips:
Set the Time.
Use Tab key to switch between Time fields.

items.name: System Date(YYYY:MM:DD)
items.tips:
Set the Date.
Use Tab key to switch between Date fields.

items.name: Serial Port1 Address
items.tips: Select settings for the Serial Port 1. If set to "Disabled", the Serial Port will not be seen by the OS.

items.name: Parallel Port Address
items.tips: Select settings for the Parallel Port. If set to "Disabled", the Parallel Port will not be seen by the OS.

items.name: Parallel Port Mode
items.tips:
Change the Parallel Port Mode. 
EPP (Enhanced Parallel Port) and ECP (Extended Capabilities Port) are two modes to transmit data by Parallel Port. EPP is more commonly used than ECP.

items.name: EPP Version
items.tips: There are differences between the two standards (1.9 and 1.7 version) which may affect the operation of devices.

items.name: ECP Mode DMA Channel
items.tips:
DMA (Direct Memory Access), a technique for transferring data from main memory to the parallel port devices without passing it through the CPU. Computers that have DMA channels can transfer data to and from devices while the CPU works on other tasks. 
Select DMA3 or DMA1 channel.

items.name: Parallel Port IRQ
items.tips: An IRQ (interrupt request) value is an assigned location where the computer can expect the parallel port controller to interrupt it when the device sends the computer signals about its operation.

items.name: USB Support
items.tips:
Select whether to enable or disable USB (Universal Seral Bus) functions.
If the functions are disabled, no USB device can be used.

items.name: USB Legacy Support
items.tips: If it is disabled, the USB keyboard and/or USB mouse may be not able to be used without device driver support.

items.name: USB Enumeration Delay
items.tips: If it is enabled, extra delay will be added when host performs USB enumeration. This may improve the compatibility of USB device detection but increase POST time.

items.name: Front USB Ports
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable the side USB ports.

items.name: Rear USB Ports
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable the rear USB ports.

items.name: SATA Controller
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable SATA controller.

items.name: SATA Drive 1
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable SATA Drive 1.

items.name: SATA Drive 2
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable SATA Drive 2.

items.name: Configure SATA as
items.tips:
Select AHCI Mode.
NOTE:
Device driver support is required  for AHCI.
Depending on how the hard disk image was installed, changing this setting may prevent the system from booting.

items.name: Hard Disk Pre-delay
items.tips: Adds a delay before the first access of a hard disk by the system software. Some hard disks hang if accessed before they have initialized themselves. This delay ensures the hard disk has initialized after power up, prior to being accessed.

items.name: UMA Frame Buffer Size
items.tips: Configure the memory size for internal graphic.

items.name: Primary Video Controller
items.tips: Select which graphic controller to be used as the primary display device.

items.name: Surround View
items.tips: If PCIE is primary display,allow IGFX(Internal Graphic) to be secondary display.

items.name: Onboard Audio Controller
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable Onboard Audio Controller

items.name: Onboard Ethernet Controller
items.tips:
Select whether to enable or disable Onboard Ethernet Controller.
NOTE: If this option is changed to "Disabled", the Intel(R) AMT related functions will be disabled.

items.name: PXE Option ROM
items.tips: Select whether to disable, load onboard PXE (Preboot Execution Environment).  This feature will allow the computer to boot from a server image.

items.name: PXE IPV4 network stack
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable PXE IPV4 network stack

items.name: PXE IPV6 network stack
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable PXE IPV6 network stack

items.name: Wireless LAN
items.tips:
Select whether to enable or disable Wireless LAN.
<Enabled> Enables use of Wireless LAN.
<Disabled> Disables use of Wireless LAN. Wireless LAN will not be available is OS.

items.name: ASPM Support
items.tips:
<Auto> Configure ASPM automatically according to what the attached device supports in each PCI Express port.
<Disabled> Disable ASPM support of all PCI Express ports.

items.name: PCIe 16x Slot Speed
items.tips: Select PCI Express port speed.

items.name: PCIe 1x Slot 1 Speed
items.tips: Select PCI Express port speed.

items.name: Card Reader
items.tips:
Select whether to enable or disable Card Reader.
<Enabled> Enables use of Card Reader.
<Disabled> Disables use of Card Reader.
Card reader will not be available in OS.

items.name: Bluetooth
items.tips:
Select whether to enable or disable Bluetooth.
<Enabled> Enables use of Bluetooth.
<Disabled> Disables use of Bluetooth.
Bluetooth will not be available in OS.

items.name: AMD Secure Virtual Machine
items.tips:
AMD Virtualization technology is a set of unique on-chip features that enables AMD PRO-based clients to run multiple operating systems and applications on a single machine.
Select whether to enable or disable AMD Virtualization technology.

items.name: CPB Mode
items.tips: Core Performance Boost allows the processor to dynamically control and adjust its operating frequency to increase performance when needed and maintain lower power and thermal characteristics during normal operation.

items.name: C6 Support
items.tips: Select whether to enable or disable the C6 power management state to minimize idle power consumption of the processor.

items.name: Dust Shield Alert
items.tips:
<Enabled> The user is reminded to clean the Dust Shield. 
<Disabled> The user is not reminded to clean the Dust Shield. 
Note that if the Dust Shield is not cleaned then it will lose its effectiveness and the machine may overheat.

items.name: After Power Loss
items.tips:
This field controls whether the system will stay on after AC power is removed and then restored.
Select "Power On" if you use a power strip to turn the system on.
Select "Power Off" if you want the system to remain off after power restored.
Select "Last State" to have the system return to the previous state.

items.name: Enhanced Power Saving Mode
items.tips:
Select whether to enable Enhanced Power Saving Mode.
<Enabled> The system will enter to Enhanced Power Saving Mode during power off. The total power consumption will be lower during power off.
<Disabled> Disables function of Enhanced Power Save Mode.
Note: When enabled Enhanced Power Saving Mode, only the Wake Up on Alarm function is supported. Other wake up functions are not supported. System will not enter to Enhanced Power Saving Mode if Intel ME is required to be active in Sx states and host is in AC mode.

items.name: ICE Performance Mode
items.tips:
<Better Acoustic Performance> The system will run with less noise at a normal thermal level.
<Better Thermal Performance> The system will run at a better thermal level with normal acoustic performance.
<Full Speed> All fans in the system will run at full speed.

items.name: ICE Thermal Alert
items.tips: Thermal monitoring & alert features to protect system under critical thermal situations.

items.name: Wake on LAN
items.tips:
Select whether to enable Wake on LAN, and/or which Startup Sequence to use after a Wake on LAN event.
NOTE: This item controls the wake up event from onboard LAN and PCI LAN.

items.name: Wake from Serial Port Ring
items.tips: Select whether to enable Wake from Serial Port Ring, and/or which Startup Sequence to use after a serial port wake event.

items.name: Wake Up on Alarm
items.tips:
Select whether to enable Wake Up on Alarm, totun on your system on a special day of the month, special day of the week or daily.
NOTE: Values in these fields may be overwritten by the operating system.

items.name: Startup Sequence
items.tips: Select the Startup Sequence to use after a Wake Up on Alarm event.

items.tips: [Enter]

items.name: Allow Flashing BIOS to a Previous Version
items.tips:
<Yes> - Flash BIOS to a previous  or current version is allowed. This is the default setting.
<No> - Flash BIOS to a previous  or current version is not allowed.

items.name: Require Admin. Pass. when Flashing
items.tips: If "No" is selected, the Adiministrator password will not be required when updating the system software.

items.name: Windows UEFI Firmware Update
items.tips:
This option enables or disables windows UEFI firmware update feature.
<Enabled> Allow windows UEFI firmware update.
<Disabled> BIOS will skip windows UEFI firmware update.

items.name: Require POP on System Boot
items.tips:
<Yes> The system prompts for passwords when the system starts from the full off or hibernate state.
<No> Passwords are not prompted and continue to boot the OS. To prevent unauthorized access to the system, recommend to set user authentication on the OS.

items.name: Require POP on Restart
items.tips: If "No" is selected, the Power-On Password will only be required when the system is started with a cold boot.

items.name: POP Changeable by User
items.tips: If "No" is selected, the Power-On Password can only be changed by the Supervisor password.

items.name: Require Admin. Pass. For F12 Boot
items.tips: If Yes and an Administrator Password is aet, the user will be prompted for a password when F12 is pressed during POST.

items.name: Smart USB Protection
items.tips:
Smart USB Protection could block copying data from the computer to the USB storage device in windows.
Read Only mode: the user can copy data from USB storage device to the Computer but cannot copy data from the computer to USB storage device.
No Access mode: the user cannot use USB storage device in windows

items.tips: [Enter]

items.name: Require HDP on System Boot
items.tips:
<Auto> - Hard Disk Password (HDP) will be required if the Hard Disk is in lock status when the system starts from the full off, hibernate or restart state.
<No> - HDP will not be required. However, HDP will be required when the hard disk is attached to a different system.

items.name: TCG Security Device
items.tips: Contains TCG security features.

items.name: Security Chip 2.0
items.tips:
<Enabled> When item enabled that TCG security feature is full function.
<Disabled> When item disabled, TCG security feature is no functional.
NOTE:
If set to  "Disabled", the TxT will be set to "Disabled" automatically.

items.name: Clear TCG Security Feature
items.tips:
Select whether to clear TCG Security Feature.
Warning: Any data in TPM will be cleared.

items.name: Physical Presence for Clear
items.tips:
This option enables or disables confirmation of a user's physical presence when Clearing the security chip. 
<Enabled> Display user confirmation screen when Clearing. 
<Disabled> No user configuration screen when Clearing.

items.name: Clear System Event Log
items.tips: [Enter]

items.name: Secure Boot
items.tips:
<Enabled> Enables Secure Boot,BIOS will prevent un-authorised OS be loaded.
<Disabled> Disables Secure Boot. 
When Secure boot set to Enabled, CSM would be automatically disabled.

items.tips: [Enter]

items.tips: [Enter]

items.tips: [Enter]

items.name: Device Guard
items.tips:
Device Guard enables PCs to be protected against malware by introducing a collective set of restrictions on a device across several technologies.
<Enabled> CPU Virtualization Technology be enabled, IOMMU, Such as Intel VT-d, AMD-Vi be enabled, Secure boot be enabled, TPM be enabled Ethernet, USB, CD, and other boot methods be disabled,only SATA device is allowed.
<Disabled>Ethernet, USB, CD, and other boot methods be enabled.

items.name: Chassis Intrusion Detection
items.tips:
Chassis Intrusion Detection is a utility that can tell whether someone has opened the case (intruded into the chassis).
NOTE:
If chassis tamper occurs, you can only enter setup to clear this error.

items.name: Configuration Change Detection
items.tips: Select whether to enable Configuration Change Detection. If enabled, when a device is installed or remove, the system will notify the user during POST. This notice can only be cleared by entering BIOS setup, saving and then exiting.

items.name: Password Count Exceeded Error
items.tips:
Select Enabled to show the POST 0199 error and prompt for password. 
Select Disabled to hide the POST 0199 error and proceed without any user action required.

items.name: CSM
items.tips:
Compatibility support Module. Permit the loading of a traditional operation system.
Enable: to support Non-UEFI operation system.
Disable: to support Win8 64-bit and later UEFI aware operation system.

items.name: Boot Mode
items.tips:
Select <Auto>, system will try to boot to UEFI or legacy operating system.
Select <UEFI Only>, system will only boot to UEFI aware operating system.
Select <Legacy Only>, system will only boot to legacy operating system.

items.name: Boot Priority
items.tips:
Select <UEFI First>, system will try to boot to UEFI OS first and then legacy OS.
Select <Legacy First>, system will try to boot to legacy OS first and then UEFI OS.

items.name: Boot Up Num-Lock Status
items.tips: This field indicates the state of the NumLock feature of the keyboard after Startup. If NumLock is "On", the keys on the keypad will act as numeric keys. If NumLock is "Off", the keys on the keypad will act as cursor keys.

items.name: Option Keys Display
items.tips:
Controls the system software option key prompts (such as F1 key) when the system is turned on. Select "Enabled" to display the prompts.
NOTE: Disabling the prompts will not affect the function of a specific key.

items.name: Option Keys Display Style
items.tips: Controls the style of prompts displayed on the POST logo screen when the system is turned on. Choosing "Normal" will prompt for the Enter key and display a menu. Choosing "Legacy" will prompt fo F1 and F12.
